clinician.trajectory_summary: A 59-year-old man presented with acute neurological symptoms including expressive aphasia, short-term memory deficits, confusion, staring spells, and right hand spasms. Neurological examination confirmed expressive aphasia and mild short-term memory loss. Initial brain MRI showed a large confluent area of signal intensity in the left medial temporal lobe and hippocampus. A repeat brain MRI demonstrated T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the left frontal and medial temporal lobe and right cingulate gyrus with minimal enhancement. CSF analysis was negative for HSV 1&2 DNA amplification, showed elevated protein, and no pleocytosis, suggesting an inflammatory or autoimmune process rather than infection.
